q: Which deep-sea fish is famous for tiny males that permanently fuse onto the much larger female's body?
note: He ends up sharing her bloodstream for life. Talk about clingy.

q: Which close cousin of the chimpanzee is famous for using sexual contact to ease tension and make up after fights?
note: Unlike chimps, bonobo females tend to hold the top social ranks.

q: What happens to a male honeybee soon after he mates with the queen in mid-air?
note: His reproductive organ breaks off inside the queen. Truly a one-and-done romance.

q: In which fish does the male carry the eggs in a belly pouch and then give birth?
note: Dads can give birth to hundreds, sometimes over a thousand, babies at once.

q: The female of which insect is notorious for sometimes eating the male during or after mating?
note: Scientists call it sexual cannibalism. Some males keep mating even after losing their heads.

q: Which animal has the biggest male member on Earth, over two metres long?
note: Relative to body size, though, much smaller creatures easily beat it.

q: To encourage breeding, some Chinese panda centres famously showed captive giant pandas what?
note: Keepers reported it helped some shy pandas get the idea.

q: A female giant panda is fertile for only about how long each year?
note: Wild pandas mostly live alone, so timing is everything.

q: Male Adélie and gentoo penguins court females by offering what small gift?
note: Nest material is precious, so a smooth one is basically a proposal.

q: During a lioness's fertile few days, roughly how often may a lion pair mate?
note: Each session lasts well under a minute, but it adds up to dozens a day.

q: Which fruit was nicknamed 'love apple' in Europe, partly from a reputation for stirring passion?
note: The French called it 'pomme d'amour'.

q: Which famous shellfish 'love food' can change between male and female during its life?
note: They are rich in zinc, a mineral important for male fertility.

q: Why do men have nipples?
a: Embryos form them before sex develops
options: Embryos form them before sex develops
note: All embryos follow the same basic body plan for their first few weeks.

q: What was the padded pouch drawing attention to the crotch of men's breeches in Tudor fashion called?
note: Some reportedly doubled as a handy pocket.

q: Which country is home to a museum dedicated to penises, with specimens from dozens of mammal species?
note: The Icelandic Phallological Museum is in the town of Húsavík.

q: Old Hollywood films under the censorship-era Production Code usually showed married couples sleeping how?
note: Many married TV couples of the 1950s also slept in twin beds on screen.

q: In the early 1950s, CBS wouldn't let the sitcom about Lucy and Ricky Ricardo say which word on air?
note: Scripts said 'expecting' instead, even though the actress playing Lucy really was.

q: On his third Ed Sullivan Show appearance in 1957, the singer nicknamed 'the King' was filmed only from where?
note: His hip-shaking moves were considered too racy for family viewers.

q: What cheeky 'club' do people supposedly join by having sex aboard a plane in flight?
note: Most airlines forbid it, and cramped toilets make membership a real challenge.

q: Which glowing bugs flash light signals from their abdomens to attract mates at night?
note: Each species has its own flash pattern, like a secret dating code.

q: When a female dog is ready to mate, she is commonly said to be 'in' what?
note: Most dogs come into it about twice a year.

q: What is the annual mating season of deer, when stags roar and clash antlers, called?
note: Stags barely eat during it and can lose a lot of weight.

q: Which small African birds are named for the strong, affectionate pair bonds they form?
note: Their genus name, Agapornis, also means 'love bird' in Greek.

q: Earthworms and most slugs have both male and female organs. What is such an animal called?
note: Two earthworms can fertilise each other at the same time.

q: Which tall African animal's males check whether a female is fertile by tasting her urine?
note: He nudges her to pee, takes a sip, then curls his lip to analyse it.

q: Which insect's adults often live only a day or so, lack working mouths and exist mainly to mate?
note: They can spend months or even years underwater as larvae before that one big day.

q: What colour is the inflatable throat pouch male frigatebirds puff up to attract females?
note: Males can keep it inflated for hours while waiting for females to fly over.

q: Whalers named a waxy oil from a certain whale's head 'spermaceti' because they mistook it for what?
note: Scientists think it helps the whale control its depth or focus sound.

q: Which furry animal, famous for multiplying fast, can conceive again within hours of giving birth?
note: A female can produce several litters every year.

q: At many Western weddings, the groom removes which item from the bride's leg and tosses it to guests?
note: It's said to have grown out of guests snatching bits of the bride's clothing for luck.

q: Male fiddler crabs wave what at passing females to attract a mate?
note: The giant claw is mostly for show; it's useless for eating.

q: During breeding season, male humpback whales are famous for producing what?
note: A single song can last around 20 minutes, and males may repeat it for hours.

q: When a female chimpanzee's rear swells up pink during her cycle, what is it signalling?
note: Scientists call them sexual swellings. Subtle, primates are not.

q: Which graceful waterbirds are famous for long-lasting pair bonds and matching neck poses during courtship?
note: Swan 'divorces' do happen, usually after failed breeding seasons.

q: Which word for a newlyweds' trip originally joked that early married sweetness would soon wane?
note: Recorded since the 1500s, the 'moon' part hinted the bliss would fade like one.

q: Relative to body size, which stuck-in-place sea crustacean has the longest male organ in the animal kingdom?
note: Up to about eight times its body length. Handy when you can never leave home.

q: Male ducks have unusually long penises. What shape are they?
note: Female ducks' reproductive tracts spiral the opposite way, an evolutionary contest.

q: Most male birds lack an external sex organ. What is their brief vent-to-vent mating contact nicknamed?
note: It is usually over almost instantly. Ducks and ostriches are among the exceptions.

q: What is a honeybee queen's mid-air mating trip, where she meets many males, called?
note: She may mate with a dozen or more males over a few flights, then never again.

q: Some land gastropods stab their partner with a sharp chalky 'arrow' before mating. What is it nicknamed?
note: The mucus it delivers improves the stabber's odds of fertilising eggs. Romance, gastropod style.

q: How many heads does the reproductive organ of a male echidna, the spiny Australian mammal, have?
note: It uses only two at a time, switching sides between sessions.

q: Female spotted hyenas have an unusually elongated sex organ that biologists nickname what?
note: Females mate and even give birth through it.

q: Roy and Silo, two male chinstrap penguins who raised a chick together, lived at which zoo?
note: Their story inspired a much-loved picture book about their chick, Tango.

q: What is unusual about the whiptail lizard species Aspidoscelis neomexicanus?
note: Eggs develop unfertilised, and mock mating between females helps trigger egg-laying.

q: What is the periodic frenzied state of bull tuskers, when fluid oozes from glands on their temples, called?
note: From Urdu 'mast', meaning intoxicated. Mahouts give such bulls a very wide berth.

q: Why does a female cat often yowl loudly at the end of mating?
a: The male's penis has backward spines
options: The male's penis has backward spines
note: Those spines also help trigger the release of her eggs.

q: Pythons, vipers and lizards have a paired sex organ and use one side at a time. What is each half called?
note: They are stored inside-out in the base of the tail when not in use.

q: How many vaginas does a female wallaby have?
note: Two lead to twin uteruses; a central canal is used for giving birth.

q: How do small male giant cuttlefish sneak past big rival males to reach females?
note: They hide their longer arms and copy female colours, then make their move.

q: Male Pisaura mirabilis, a European nursery web species, often courts a female by offering what?
note: Some cheeky males wrap up a worthless dud gift instead.

q: Male house mice court females with what, mostly too high-pitched for humans to hear?
note: Researchers found the calls contain repeated phrases, much like birdsong.

q: Darwin wrote in 1860 that gazing at which bird's tail made him feel sick?
note: The showy tail helped push him toward his theory of sexual selection.

q: Legend says which Aztec ruler drank goblets of frothy cacao for stamina before visiting his many wives?
note: European chroniclers spread the tale; historians treat it as more legend than fact.

q: Which snack is named after a 19th-century American diet reformer who believed plain food curbed lust?
note: Today's sugary versions would probably horrify him.

q: An old Malay saying goes: 'When the ___ falls, the sarong goes up.' Which fruit?
note: The spiky, pungent fruit has a long folk reputation for putting people in the mood.

q: The herb Epimedium, sold as a sex-drive booster, is better known by what cheeky common name?
note: Legend says a herder noticed his goats getting frisky after grazing on it.

q: Which Andean root from Peru is widely sold as a natural sex-drive booster?
note: Nicknamed 'Peruvian ginseng'; a few small studies hint at modest effects.

q: In the 18th-century American colonies, courting couples sometimes shared a bed fully clothed, with a board between. What was this called?
note: Some parents added a sack tied around one partner's legs, just to be sure.

q: The Cerne Abbas Giant, a chalk hill figure with very visible manhood, is in which UK county?
note: Local legend says couples hoping for a baby should spend a night on it.

q: Jeju Loveland, an open-air park of erotic sculptures, is on an island belonging to which country?
note: It opened in 2004 and became a popular stop for newlyweds.

q: If a clownfish group's breeding female disappears, what does the largest male do?
note: All clownfish start life as male. Pixar skipped that plot twist.

q: Which Australasian bird's males build decorated display structures from twigs to woo females?
note: Satin males collect objects of one favourite colour, even drinking straws and clothes pegs.

q: How does a male North American porcupine court a female?
options: He sings to her at dawn
note: If she's interested, she relaxes her spines. Carefully does it.

q: The males of which small bird famously 'moonwalk' backwards along a branch to impress females?
note: They also make sharp snapping sounds with their wings.

q: What do male betta fish build at the surface to hold a female's eggs?
note: Dad then guards the eggs, catching any that sink and spitting them back into the nest.

q: Female swine were traditionally used to find which luxury delicacy hidden in woodland soil, partly because it smells like a boar's sex scent?
note: Many hunters now use dogs, which are less tempted to gobble the prize.

q: A popular story links the slang 'hooker' to US Civil War general Joseph Hooker. What's the truth?
a: The word was in print before the war
options: The word was in print before the war
He coined it in a speech
A cartoonist named it after him
note: It was recorded in the 1840s, probably from 'hook', as in to snare customers.

q: Many reef corals off Queensland spawn together on nights timed to follow what?
note: The synchronised release looks like an underwater snowstorm.

q: What is the communal display ground called where males, like sage grouse, gather to show off for females?
note: Females stroll through, compare the talent, and most pick the same few stars.

q: Some marine flatworms, each with both sexes, duel to decide who gets inseminated. What is this nicknamed?
note: The loser takes on the costly job of producing the eggs.

q: Camels, ferrets and alpacas release eggs only after mating, not on a regular cycle. What is this called?
note: Mating itself triggers the surge that releases the eggs.

q: The slime mould Physarum polycephalum is often said to have how many 'sexes' (mating types)?
note: Its mating-type genes combine in hundreds of ways. A French zoo exhibited it as 'the blob'.

q: In 1989, what did the US FDA conclude about over-the-counter products sold as sex-drive boosters?
options: They worked but cost too much
note: Placebo and mood still do a lot of the heavy lifting.

q: An Ig Nobel award went to research testing which famous fizzy drink as a spermicide?
note: One study said it worked, another said it didn't. Do not try this at home.

q: A 2021 Ig Nobel award went to a study finding an orgasm works about as well as which medicine?
note: The effect lasted up to about an hour.

q: An ancient Egyptian pregnancy test had a woman urinate on seeds of which two grains?
note: Sprouting meant a baby was on the way. A 1963 test found it surprisingly accurate.

q: Romans wore phallus-shaped charms called 'fascinum' against the evil eye. Which modern word shares that root?
note: It first meant to hold someone spellbound; 'deeply interest' arrived around 1815.

q: What is the name for a pubic wig, worn historically and sometimes by actors today?
note: Records of the word go back to the 1600s.

q: What were the secret 1700s taverns and meeting places for gay men in the British capital called?
note: 'Molly' was period slang for a gay or effeminate man.

q: What is the curled-upper-lip grimace goats, camels and zebras make to analyse scents like mating signals called?
note: It channels scent to a special organ in the roof of the mouth.

q: Male bedbugs skip the usual route and pierce the female's abdomen to mate. What is this called?
note: Females evolved a special patch of tissue at the usual piercing spot to limit damage.

q: What is the specially modified arm a male cephalopod, such as a squid, uses to mate?
note: In argonauts the arm detaches inside the female; naturalists once mistook it for a parasitic worm.

q: During mating, a male damselfly can first use his genitals to do what?
note: That way the eggs she lays are more likely to be his.

q: Leopard slugs famously mate while doing what?
a: Hanging from a rope of slime
options: Hanging from a rope of slime
note: They twirl around each other in mid-air, sometimes for hours.

q: In the dark deep sea, how do male Octopoteuthis deletron squid seem to handle rare encounters?
a: Mating with males and females alike
options: Mating with males and females alike
note: Telling sexes apart in pitch black is hard, so they don't risk missing a chance.

q: A 2019 Ig Nobel award honoured research on scrotal temperature asymmetry in clothed and unclothed workers of which job?
note: The researchers were French, and so were the postmen.

q: What is the only human cell with a whip-like tail to propel itself?
note: It's also one of the smallest cells in the body.

q: Male white-spotted puffers in Japan attract females by building what on the seabed?
note: Divers spotted the mysterious circles for years before catching the fish at work.

q: Male common nightingales famously sing through the night. Who are these night-time songs mainly aimed at?
note: Once a male pairs up, his night singing usually stops. Mission accomplished.

q: Which small, colourful aquarium fish gives birth to live young and is nicknamed the 'millions fish'?
note: A female can produce several broods from a single mating.

q: A group of females that mate with one dominant male, as in gorillas or sea lions, is called what?
note: Dominant male sea lions may guard a dozen or more females at once.

q: Which Australian bird's males mimic sounds like camera shutters and chainsaws in their courtship displays?
note: Males also dance on cleared mounds, fanning their spectacular tails over their heads.

q: Male bighorn sheep compete for females mainly by doing what?
note: Clashes can go on for hours; their reinforced heads absorb the shock.

q: Which Indian bird's males weave hanging nests that females inspect before choosing a mate?
note: Males often start several nests, and a female picks the best-built one.

q: The name 'ginseng', a root long sold for vigour, comes from Chinese words meaning what?
note: The forked root often looks like a little human figure.

q: To attract females, male hooded seals inflate what?
a: A balloon-like membrane from one nostril
options: A balloon-like membrane from one nostril
note: They can also inflate a black hood on top of their head.

q: What is the Victorian practice of sending coded messages of love through chosen blooms called?
note: Different blooms, and even their colours, carried particular meanings, so bouquets needed careful reading.

q: After mating, the sea slug Chromodoris reticulata does what with its male organ?
a: Sheds it and has another ready
options: Sheds it and has another ready
note: It can mate again within about a day, thanks to a coiled internal reserve.

q: In phalaropes, brightly coloured females court the males, who then incubate the eggs. What is this called?
note: Female phalaropes may pair with several males in a season.

q: The word 'fornicate' comes from Latin 'fornix'. What did 'fornix' originally mean?
note: Roman sex workers were said to solicit under arched vaults, so the word drifted.
